text: Is my easy pace too fast?

No, your easy pace looks well placed. Your easy runs sit at 5:42-5:50/km (4-week average 5:47/km), in the middle of the 5:11-6:13/km easy band. They are even, with every km split nearly identical, and average HR is 137-140 bpm. That is roughly 65% of your heart rate reserve (max 188, rest 52), which is properly easy. Cadence is steady at 174 spm.

The one thing to watch is the long runs. Average HR has gone 142 (16 km, 5:47/km), then 143 (17 km, 5:50/km), then 146 (18.6 km, 5:52/km). Pace got slightly slower while HR rose, and efficiency slipped from 1.200 to 1.169. The 18.6 km run had 186 m of climbing, and distance also grew, so some drift is expected. It is a trend to keep an eye on, not a reason to slow down or change anything.

None of your runs have an RPE logged, so I can only judge effort from HR and pace. If you add an RPE (easy should feel around 3-4 out of 10), I can tell you whether the HR creep matches how it feels.

text: Swap Thursday and Saturday next week please, I'm travelling Thursday.

I can do that. Week 5 currently has the 4 × 0.8 km intervals (4:09/km) plus Strength B on Thursday 3 Dec, and the easy 8 km on Saturday 5 Dec. I'll propose swapping them: intervals and Strength B go to Saturday, the easy 8 km goes to Thursday, and volumes stay the same.

There are two trade-offs. First, intervals on Saturday put a hard session the day before the 16.6 km long run on Sunday 6 Dec, so you'll start the long run with tired legs. Keep the long run truly easy at 5:11-6:13/km and it should be fine, but it is a bit more load on the achilles than the usual spacing. Second, the easy 8 km lands on Thursday, the day you're travelling. If you can't fit it in, tell me and I can propose dropping or moving it. I can't add a fifth run, since you're capped at 4 runs a week.

Separately, nothing is logged since the 18.6 km long run on 22 Nov, so Tuesday 24 Nov's easy run looks missed. If that was deliberate rest, fine. If something is going on, let me know before Thursday's intervals this week.
